title: The first game I made with AI!
author: LightToyInteractives
selftext: I made a cozy market management game, hope you enjoy it (unless you bankrupt your shop, of course)!Can you tell at a glance what the game is about? Did you figure out the game's mechanics right away?

comments.author: XXIIIOIIIXX
comments.body: how hard is it to get your game on the play store? i heard now you have to beta test it?

replies.author: LightToyInteractives
replies.body:
Here's how it went for me, step by step.

**1. Internal testing.** Before anything else there's an internal testing track. It's where you upload early builds of your game and test them yourself, and while setting up the app you also fill in the required forms (privacy policy and so on). This stage only took me a day or two. After that you move on to closed testing.

**2. Closed testing (the 14-day part).** Google requires at least 12 testers to take part in your closed test for 14 days, and they're expected to open the game and do something in it every day. From what I've seen, people find their 12 testers on Reddit, Telegram, and tester-swap groups. The problem is that testers usually join in the first few days and then stop opening the app. When that happens you either get rejected and have to redo the 14 days, or the counter resets. I saw several people get stuck here and restart the 14 days three or four times.

In my case, I found a website that charged about $10 (paid in my local currency). For that they provided 12 testers for 14 days and promised to get my app through closed testing. It worked for me.

**3. Production access form.** After closed testing ends, a form appears that you have to fill out before you can apply for production. It asks about your testing process. The service I used sent me answers for it.

**4. Review.** Google reviewed my form, which took 3 days. Then I got permission to apply for production.

**5. Production release.** I applied, uploaded my latest version, and it was approved in 2 days.

**Total time:** about 19-20 days from when I wanted to publish until the game was live. That's longer than I'd have liked, but I used the time to keep improving the game, so it actually worked out.

**After launch:** my updates have been published within about an hour, which I really liked.
